title: The negation trap: do concept probes flip when the safety statement is negated?

original_idea.body: The negation trap: train safety concept-vector probe on affirmatives, test on negations, measure accuracy collapse. Linear probing on open model.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: negation-fragile safety probes are trivially evaded, directly undermining monitoring reliability (level 4).

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Linear probing on matched affirmative/negated sets; ideal beginner stats exercise (level 5).

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped single experiment (train on affirmatives, test on negations) with clear success metric (level 5).

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Independent-friendly probe robustness audit on open models, neglected by labs (level 4).

low_compute.reasoning: Linear probing on cached activations, near CPU/free-tier (level 5).

novelty.reasoning: Negation-collapse documented for truth probes; extending to safety concept probes may be partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Negation fragility known broadly; the safety-probe-specific test may be open.
